name: scenario_generator_output
description: Return the generated edge-case scenarios. Use this tool for every response: it is the only way to deliver scenarios.

AdversarialScenarioDraft.description:
`adversarial`: both numbers are asked for, neither is forced above 1.

Replay and double-submit need `repeat`, but the category is wider than that
— ordering tricks and malformed sequences probe abuse without sending the
action twice. Forcing `repeat >= 2` here would push every adversarial
scenario into one shape. The set-level check
(`ScenarioSetDraft.missing_execution_modes`) is what catches a writing set
in which nothing replays.

repeat.description: Send the action N times in sequence. Above 1 for replay or double-submit; 1 for abuse that does not need a duplicate. (maximum: 50, minimum: 1)
repeat.title: Repeat

concurrency.description: Send the action N times in parallel (race). 1 = no race. (maximum: 50, minimum: 1)
concurrency.title: Concurrency

id.description: Stable id, lowercase slug, e.g. 'sc-001' or 'sc-overdraft'.
id.title: Id

title.description: One short line naming what is probed.
title.title: Title

rationale.description: Why this is worth testing — the failure mode it would expose.
rationale.title: Rationale

Expectation.description: What a correct system would do — never what the buggy target does.

expected_status.description: HTTP status codes a correct implementation may return for the action.
expected_status.title: Expected Status

expected_behavior.description: One or two sentences on correct behaviour, in terms a reviewer can check against the recorded response. Used by the LLM judge.
expected_behavior.title: Expected Behavior

invariants.description: Checkable statements about state after the action, e.g. 'sum of both balances is unchanged'. Verified against `probes` output.
invariants.title: Invariants

probes.description: Read-only calls run after the action to observe resulting state.
probes.title: Probes

Expectation.title: Expectation

HttpStep.description: `HttpStep` as the generator writes it: every field present, nothing free-form.

name.description: Short snake_case label, unique within the scenario.
name.title: Name

body.description: The JSON request body, written as JSON text of an object, e.g. '{"owner": "alice", "amount": 10}'. Empty string when the call has no body. String values inside may use {placeholders}.
body.title: Body

save.description: Capture values from this step's JSON response for later steps: {"name": "src_id", "value": "id"} reads the response field `id` and binds it to {src_id}. Dotted paths index nested objects, e.g. 'data.account.id'. [] when nothing is captured.
save.title: Save

PlainScenarioDraft.description:
The other five categories: neither number appears in the schema at all.

Requiring both on every scenario asked the model for 28 numbers at the
default quota, 24 of which could only sensibly be 1, and it omitted some
often enough to cost an attempt — with a02's DomainModel in the prompt, no
generation validated on its first try. Asking only where the number is the
point cuts that to 8 (measured in CHANGELOG › Measured).

Code supplies 1 and 1 on the way to `Scenario`.

StressScenarioDraft.description:
`stress`: a race is what the category probes, so `concurrency` must be above 1.

A `stress` scenario left at `concurrency: 1` is a single request with a
label — the generator has produced exactly that, including one titled "Many
parallel transfers racing". Here the schema does not merely ask for the
number, it rules out the value that makes the category a lie.

concurrency.description: How many copies of the action run at once. Must be 2 or more: one sequential request cannot expose a race. (maximum: 50, minimum: 2)

input_schema.description:
The generator's wire format — just the scenarios.

This is what the model fills in via the forced tool call; run metadata
(target, model, timestamp) is attached by code afterwards, so the model
cannot get it wrong. `extra="forbid"` turns silent field drift into a
validation error the retry can act on.
